page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose cloud virtual machine instance powered by a 32-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 CPU running at 3.4 GHz. It features a 1:1 physical core to vCPU ratio without multithreading, along with 128 GB of RAM (4 GB per vCPU), a 128 MB L3 cache, and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core. The instance has no integrated local SSD storage, relying instead on attached Premium Storage solutions for persistent disk volumes, and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory sub-system performance, with uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 450.97 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth achieving 188.48 GB/sec. The instance delivers strong multi-core execution metrics, registering 66,298.79 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 19,998 in Geekbench multi-core workloads. In database operations, PassMark benchmarks place the server in the top tier, complemented by high web serving throughput of 52.72 GB/sec and 61.71 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core CPU scores and large-scale LLM prompt processing remain within average to lower categories.

By leveraging an ARM-based Neoverse-N2 architecture, the D32ps_v6 offers high resource density and strong multi-core capability at favorable hardware cost efficiency compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced baseline for parallel compute tasks. Optimal workload fits include relational and key-value databases, web serving clusters, microservices, and software compilation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs. Equipped with 128 GB of RAM, 128 MB of L3 cache, and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, the instance operates without bundled local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, depending on external Premium Storage for block device management. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier memory bandwidth, achieving 450.97 GB/sec uncached read throughput, alongside top-tier database performance metrics and PassMark memory ratings. Multi-core performance is strong across synthetic tests, static web serving throughput reaching 52.72 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 61 million operations per second. While single-threaded processing remains average, the high density of dedicated physical cores renders the instance highly cost-efficient for scaled multi-threaded tasks. It is well suited for containerized microservices, web server pools, database hosting, software build systems, and general compute workloads.
